name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Indonesia's rupiah hit a record low of 18,250 per dollar on 13 Nov despite intervention; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: Indonesia's rupiah fell to a record 18,250 per dollar on 13 Nov, down more than 8.5% this year, as Fed rate-rise bets and political uncertainty weighed; Bank Indonesia said it had intervened (Business Recorder). The Turkish lira has traded near a record low of about 50 per dollar in a managed depreciation since early November. Neither has fallen 10% in a month, and searches on 15 Nov found no major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support.
for_you: Travellers and firms dealing in Indonesian rupiah or Turkish lira face weaker exchange rates and higher local inflation. There is no wider emerging-market crisis for now.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month (rupiah down ~8.5% year to date), no default or emergency IMF support

sources.title: Business Recorder — Indonesian rupiah hits record low as dollar rally
Bloomberg — Indonesian rupiah drops to record amid MSCI concerns, oil risks

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
